headline: Trump bans three outlets from the White House
summary: He announced it Friday on Truth Social, saying the three outlets "constantly write or report fiction or lies" and giving no examples. He did not say how the ban would work, and reporters from CNN and Politico were still on the grounds afterward. Asked why now, he said, "You get sick of it." He said a court may not let it stand.

cover_question.q: Can the president ban the news?

cover_answer: He says so. Last time CNN sued, and got its reporter back.
table_question: If someone keeps saying bad things about you, can you shut them out?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president said three news companies can't come to his workplace, the White House, anymore. He says they say untrue things about him, but he didn't say which ones. Reporters tell everyone what the president does, like the kid who tells the class what happened at recess. The grown-ups are sorting out whether he can do that.
5-7.why: At five, the news is a person who tells you what happened. The rule fight is for later.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: On Friday Trump wrote that CNN, MS NOW and Politico are banned from the White House for "fiction or lies." He gave no examples, and CNN and Politico reporters were still there. Like a player sent off without hearing the foul; a court may get asked.
8-12.why: A punishment with no stated reason is a fairness call for them.

13-17.script: Should a president pick which reporters cover him? Trump says CNN, MS NOW and Politico are out over "cumulative stories over the last few years," and said a court may not let it stand. Who checks the most powerful person?
13-17.why: He has a grievance, and the rule matters more. Let them hold both.

5-7.q: Why is the president mad at the news?
5-7.a: He says they tell lies about him. He didn't say which stories. Reporters' job is to watch what he does and ask hard questions.

8-12.q: Can the president ban the news?
8-12.a: He says he can. The article says it's unclear how it would work, and the outlets are likely to sue.
He says they report "fiction or lies" but gave no examples. Asked why now, he said, "You get sick of it."

13-17.q: Isn't that against the First Amendment?
13-17.a: Press groups are expected to sue. He said himself it's worth doing "whether it survives or doesn't."
Yes. In his first term he banned a CNN reporter; CNN sued and got the pass back. AP sued over a 2025 ban; that case is ongoing.
